chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqutini, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dhuraih ibn Yazid al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Poverty is the red death. It was said: Is poverty from dinars and dirhams? He said: No, however, it is from religion.

key_terms.الْفَقْرُ: Poverty, specifically spiritual or religious deficiency in this context
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ الْأَحْمَرُ: The red death, a metaphor for the destructive nature of religious poverty

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between material poverty and spiritual poverty in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishing between material destitution and spiritual bankruptcy, identifying the latter as the 'red death' due to its fatal consequence for the soul. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia theology, where *Din* (religion/faith) is viewed as the essential life force; its absence renders a person spiritually dead despite physical existence. The metaphor of 'red death' likely alludes to the blood of martyrdom or the severity of the soul's demise, emphasizing that true ruin is the loss of divine connection rather than worldly assets.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammed bin Isa bin Ubaid al-Yaqteeni, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Dhuraih bin Yazid al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
Poverty is the red death. It was said: Poverty from dinars and dirhams? He said: No, however, from religion.
